skill.name: product-design-harness
skill.description: Use when a product direction, feature, workflow, experiment, launch, feedback signal, automation, or scale decision needs judgment before execution or the next iteration.
skill.summary: Review product decisions through user needs, evidence quality, and business viability before authorizing bounded work.
skill.author: cis2042

content.value_statement: Product teams can build quickly before testing their assumptions. This skill reviews user needs, evidence, and business viability to define a bounded next step.
actual_capabilities: Select Quick Gate, Standard Gate, or UX3 Council based on scope, uncertainty, risk, and reversibility.
Review User Flow, Evidence Flow, and Business Flow, then select the worst verdict and deterministic weakest flow.
Decompose product directions into testable claims with dependencies, counter-evidence, and stop conditions.
Produce continue, verify, or stop_reframe outcomes with explicit execution boundaries and human decision requirements.
Create bounded context packs after continue reviews and validate matching review and handoff fields with bundled Python scripts.
Organize independent council reviews, challenge rounds, and structured red-team reviews for unanimous continue decisions.
limitations: Evidence quality depends on supplied sources; validation scripts cannot establish that research claims are true.
External evidence retrieval requires separately available tools or connectors; the bundled routing helper is offline.
Human owners must decide taste, ethics, strategy, and acceptable risk; the skill does not replace accountable approval.
Python validators require jsonschema and referencing dependencies; review boundaries do not provide operating-system access enforcement.

use_cases.title: Assess a Feature Request
use_cases.description: Review a proposed feature against user problems, supporting evidence, ownership cost, and the smallest useful test.

use_cases.title: Challenge a Prototype Direction
use_cases.description: Separate interview opinions from observed behavior and identify assumptions that require a focused prototype test.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Bounded Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Validate an approved review and matching context pack before assigning implementation work to coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Product Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product direction: [direction]. Current evidence: [sources]. Owner and organization: [details]. Select a mode and list missing intake. Do not implement.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: clarify a request before choosing the next step.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Standard Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Run Standard Gate for [feature] at [stage]. Use [brief and evidence]. Review all three flows independently. Return the canonical review with boundaries and stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess a new feature or workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a Risky Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Run UX3 Council for [decision]. Use [brief, evidence receipts, and owner]. Decompose claims, review lanes independently, and complete challenge rounds. Red-team unanimous continue results before synthesis.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate uncertainty, stakeholder conflict, or material risk.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [continue review] to create a matching context pack. Copy scope and controls exactly. Validate both artifacts with the bundled checker. Report failures without implementing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare reviewed scope for a coding agent.

output_examples.input: Review weekly report exports requested through support tickets, without evidence of managers' current reporting behavior.
output: Missing proof: recurring reporting work and the cost of the current workaround.
Next action: test a static report sample during workflow interviews.
Boundary: no scheduled exports, live customer data access, or external delivery.

output_examples.input: Review a proposed product direction supported only by untraceable founder impressions.
output: Reason: no traceable signal supports the core problem.
Reframed question: which specific actor experiences a recurring problem that can be observed?
Boundary: research and reframing only; no implementation handoff.

output_examples.input: Prepare an implementation handoff from an approved continue review and its linked evidence receipts.
output: Handoff: context pack linked to the approved review.
Scope: exact copy of the review's allowed actions.
Controls: preserve approval gates, prohibited actions, unresolved assumptions, and stop conditions.
Validation: check the review and context pack together before implementation.

best_practices: Provide traceable evidence, counter-signals, affected stakeholders, and a named accountable owner before requesting a decision.
Choose the smallest responsible review mode and keep human judgment separate from evidence tiers.
Validate review artifacts and linked context packs together; review again when scope, data, risk, or stakeholders change.
anti_patterns: Treating quotes, simulated users, or internal confidence as proof of real behavior.
Averaging reviewer verdicts or removing counter-evidence to obtain approval.
Turning a verify result into general implementation work or expanding an approved context pack.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews product directions, features, workflows, experiments, launches, automation, and scaling decisions through user, evidence, and business perspectives.

faq.question: Which review mode should I use?
faq.answer: Use Quick Gate for small reversible changes, Standard Gate for new features, and UX3 Council for high uncertainty or meaningful risk.

faq.question: What outcomes can a review return?
faq.answer: Continue permits a bounded handoff, verify permits one proof step, and stop_reframe returns a better product question.

faq.question: Does the skill collect research automatically?
faq.answer: It defines evidence request and receipt contracts. Actual retrieval requires available tools or connectors; the bundled routing helper makes no model calls.

faq.question: Do valid review artifacts prove that a decision is safe?
faq.answer: No. Validators check structure and selected consistency rules. They do not verify evidence truth, grant human approvals, or enforce runtime permissions.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundle provides Markdown instructions, schemas, examples, and Python validators. Your runtime must supply agent orchestration and any external tools.
